72	  reads (streamed ext bytes + the `0x20` calibration) is decrypted with that key, so
73	  plaintext reads as garbage. The base Wiimote captures the key, derives the ft/sb
74	  tables, and encrypts outgoing ext data (streamed bytes at reg offset `0x08`; reg

92	is a second front-end beside the CLI: a UART1 task (Feather RX=`GPIO7`/TX=`GPIO8`,
93	1 Mbaud) that parses framed messages (`mf_proto.h`: `SOF/TYPE/LEN/CRC8`) and drives
94	the existing `Wiimote_*`/`Guitar_*`/`Fauxmote_*` APIs — `GUITAR` (fret/strum/whammy/
95	aux), `WIIMOTE` (core/D-pad/stick, via new `Guitar_SetStick`), `LINK_CMD`, planned

97	200 ms link watchdog reverts all inputs to safe defaults when the link goes quiet.
98	**On hardware: builds, boots, and the Wii connects with the link task running.**
99	Not yet driven by marvin (that's the next side). Wire protocol: `docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md`.
100	
101	**Link stability (done):** idle disconnects are fixed — Bluedroid's JV idle→sniff
102	delay (default 5 s) is overridden to 65 s via a `-D BTA_FTC_OPS_IDLE_TO_SNIFF_DELAY_MS`
103	in the top-level CMake (`#ifndef`'d `#define`; the timeout field is UINT16 + a 197 ms
104	offset, so stay < ~65338). With sniff effectively off the link stays active (Wii keeps
105	polling), so no supervision timeouts and no BTA PM-slot leak (the leak that previously
106	forced a power-cycle). **Auto-reconnect was removed** (2026-06-13): it didn't survive
107	the GH3 launch and is the wrong tool for keep-awake. Recovery from an unexpected drop
108	is now the explicit `reconnect` command; keep-awake is better served by occasional
109	input/state changes (which Marvin's command stream provides during use).
110	
111	**OPEN — GH3 game-launch handoff (needs a BT sniffer):** when a game disc boots, the
112	Wii goes HID-silent toward fauxmote for many seconds, then drops the link (`rsn 0x08`).
113	A manual `reconnect` re-establishes the link, but the session isn't reliably usable in-game.
114	A real Wiimote rides the handoff with a quick ~2 s LED off/on. fauxmote's own logs
115	don't show *why* the Wii goes silent on us vs a real Wiimote — there's no command we
116	visibly mishandle (zero RX reports during the gap). Diagnosing needs a Bluetooth
117	sniffer to diff a real Wiimote vs fauxmote through the GH3 launch. **Workaround for
118	now: restart fauxmote after the game has started** (a fresh boot reconnects cleanly).
119	The recurring `mode 3 … BASIC mode` reconnect warning is likely a red herring (real
120	Wiimotes use Basic-mode L2CAP for HID). Revisit after the guitar extension — GH3 may
121	engage the controller differently once it sees a guitar.
122	
123	**Other notes:**
124	- **Keep-awake:** the Wii idle-disconnects on lack of *input*; streaming reports +
125	  occasional button activity keeps it alive (free during gameplay).
126	- **Caveat:** a Wiimote cannot power a Wii on from standby (BT radio off); "wake" only
127	  means reconnecting while the console is already running.

133	## Decision log
134	
135	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
136	|------|----------|-----------|
137	| 2026-07-02 | **marvin↔fauxmote link = UART first, layered message protocol (spec: [`docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md`](../../../docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md)).** Three layers: transport-agnostic message layer (`TYPE`+fixed payload), a UART framing layer (`SOF 0x7E`/`TYPE`/`LEN`/`CRC8`), UART PHY (1 Mbaud 8-N-1 on a **second** UART, not the CDC console). Messages are **independent state-slice updaters**: `GUITAR` (3 B hot: fret/strum mask + whammy + aux), `WIIMOTE` (4 B nav: core buttons/D-pad/stick), plus planned `ACCEL` (3 B, tilt→star power) and `POINTER` (3 B, IR) slices, `LINK_CMD` (1 B: pair/stop/reconnect/unlink/ext), and `STATUS` (4 B f→m). fauxmote latches each slice and assembles the Wii report from all of them; each slice is absolute/latest-wins. A **single** 200 ms link watchdog (reset by any control message) reverts *all* slices to safe defaults when the link goes fully quiet. `GUITAR` byte 0 is bit-identical to marvin's T1S guitar mask. The link is a second front-end over the existing `Wiimote_*`/`Guitar_*`/`Fauxmote_*` APIs (a `marvin_link.c` beside the CLI). | Primary purpose is low-latency GH gameplay, so the hot path is one tiny fixed message with no handshake/ack. Absolute state matches both ends (marvin's bitmask + fauxmote's ~15 ms streaming) and self-heals dropped frames. Layering keeps the message bytes identical when the transport later moves to T1S — only the framing binding changes (Ethernet FCS replaces `SOF`/`CRC`). Reusing the CLI's module APIs avoids duplicating any behavior. Resolves Q5. |
138	| 2026-06-13 | **Removed the persistent auto-reconnect task; recovery is the manual `reconnect` command only.** Drops just reset state (`Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected`); no automatic re-initiation. | Auto-reconnect neither survived the GH3 game-launch handoff nor served as a keep-awake mechanism (reconnecting ≠ staying awake). Keeping the Wii awake is better done with occasional input/state changes, which Marvin's command stream provides during use. Removing it also drops the slot-leak/backoff complexity. The sniff-delay override (idle→sniff = 65 s) stays — that genuinely prevents idle supervision-timeout drops. |
139	| 2026-06-13 | **Extension encryption is mandatory for GH3 and implemented in the base Wiimote (`ext_crypto.c`); the guitar module stays plaintext.** GH3's real key handshake (register trace): `0x55`→`0xf0` (disable) → read ID `0xfa` in clear → `0xAA`→`0xf0` (enable) → 16-byte key to `0x40`-`0x4f`. The base captures the key, derives ft/sb, and encrypts outgoing ext data (streamed bytes @ offset `0x08`; reg reads @ `addr & 7`). | Everything GH3 reads from the extension is decrypted with that key, so plaintext is garbage (the "green/red worked unencrypted" observation was a decryption coincidence). Encryption is a generic Wiimote feature (nunchuk/classic encrypt too), so it belongs in the base, not the guitar. Corrects the plan's guess that GH3 used the old `0→0x40` init. |
140	| 2026-06-13 | **Cipher tables come from Dolphin's 1st-party set, not `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator`'s `wm_crypto.c`.** rnconrad's S-boxes are corrupted (sbox[3]@0x60, [4]@0xd8, [6]@0x88/0xec are `0xD0`/`0xF0` & `0xD2`/`0xE2` transcription flips → not valid permutations). Used Dolphin's `keygen_sbox_1st_party` + `sboxes_1st_party[8]`; verified the key-schedule/encrypt algorithm term-for-term against Dolphin and round-tripped GH3's real key (idx 0, encrypt→decrypt identity). | Wrong table bytes silently corrupt the keystream → undebuggable "notes are garbage." Dolphin is GPL and validated against real games; the marcan tables are reverse-engineered hardware constants (facts), reproduced with our own code. |
141	| 2026-06-13 | **Guitar is a self-registering extension module behind `wiimote_ext.h`; `wiimote.c` is extension-agnostic.** `wiimote_extension_t` = register bank + `build_report`/`set_button`/`reset`; `Wiimote_RegisterExtension`. Buttons drive by name via `Wiimote_SetButton`/`TapButton`. | Plans for other extensions (nunchuk/classic) as drop-in `*.c` files, keeps the base generic, and keeps the CLI as thin pass-throughs over the same API Marvin will use. |
142	| 2026-06-13 | **Byte0/1 bits 7-6 must be set (GH3 Les Paul ident); single IR calibration kept.** Clear ident bits make GH3 treat us as a GHWT guitar and ignore the strum bar. Basic-IR pointer is correct on the main Wii screen with the same calibration as extended; the GH3-internal Home-overlay mis-scaling is GH3's own transform and is moot (IR is physically blocked when the Wiimote is in the guitar — guitar-mode Home nav uses the analog stick). | Found by hardware testing. No second/basic-mode calibration: the format packing is provably identical to extended (Dolphin + Linux), so the only real difference (GH3) isn't ours to fix and doesn't matter on real hardware. |
143	| 2026-06-12 | **`esp_hidd` is a dead end for Wii emulation; the only working ESP-IDF path is a custom SDP record (internal Bluedroid `SDP_*` API) + raw L2CAP HID on PSM 0x11/0x13 (`esp_bt_l2cap`), with the hardcoded SDP buffer raised.** Two independent walls: (1) the Wii rejects esp_hidd's record even with a small descriptor (wrong HID attribute values — subclass/reconnect-initiate/etc., which esp_hidd hardcodes and doesn't expose); (2) the real 217-byte descriptor can't even be registered — `SDP_MAX_PAD_LEN` (the per-record attribute pad) is **hardcoded 300** (`sdp_db.c:495`, `bluedroid_user_config.h`; no menuconfig), and the full Wiimote record is ~463 B → `SDP_AddAttribute fail … ID 518`. Confirmed feasible building blocks in IDF v6.0.1: `SDP_CreateRecord`/`SDP_AddAttribute`/`SDP_AddSequence` (private `stack/sdp_api.h`) and `esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(psm)`. | Bluedroid is the only Classic-BT stack on ESP32, and its public APIs can't host an arbitrary SDP record (`esp_sdp` RAW is search-only). So the path requires *unsupported internals*: raise `SDP_MAX_PAD_LEN` via an injected `CONFIG_BT_SDP_PAD_LEN` compile define, build the exact Wiimote record with the internal SDP DB API, skip esp_hidd, and serve HID over raw L2CAP + hand-rolled HIDP. Heavy + fragile across IDF updates, but it's the real route. The exact 463-byte record + 217-byte descriptor are saved at [`wiimote-sdp.md`](wiimote-sdp.md). |
144	| 2026-06-12 | **Q1 resolved: ESP-IDF `esp_hidd`'s auto-generated SDP record is NOT accepted by the Wii → pivot to raw L2CAP (listen on PSM 0x11 control / 0x13 data) + a hand-built SDP record matching a real Wiimote.** Verbose Bluedroid logs: the Wii opens an ACL link, connects to our SDP server (PSM 1), reads our records (we send 14/250/37-byte SDP responses), then disconnects the SDP channel and terminates the ACL (`rsn 0x13` = remote user terminated) **without ever opening the HID PSMs**. SSP was confirmed off this round (legacy pairing) and discovery works (limited-discoverable + COD `0x002504`), so SDP content is the only remaining blocker. Wii BD_ADDR observed: `00:17:ab:07:2c:21`. | The Wii validates the SDP record against a real Wiimote's; esp_hidd's generic HID record (right VID/PID, wrong attributes + HID descriptor) fails the check, so it never proceeds to HID. Matches why `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator` replaces the host BT stack to serve the exact SDP. Open: whether ESP-IDF lets us serve a fully custom SDP record (esp_sdp API vs internal Bluedroid `SDP_*` API) and listen on the fixed HID PSMs via `esp_bt_l2cap`. |
145	| 2026-06-12 | **Phase 1 first attempt uses ESP-IDF's unified `esp_hidd` BT-classic HID device wearing the Wiimote identity, not a hand-rolled raw-L2CAP/SDP stack.** `bt_hid_device.c`: `esp_hidd_dev_init(ESP_HID_TRANSPORT_BT)` with VID `0x057e`/PID `0x0306`/version `0x0100`/name `Nintendo RVL-CNT-01`, COD set to `0x002504` (peripheral/joystick), a minimal vendor-defined report map (just report IDs 0x30 in / 0x12 out), **SSP disabled** (`CONFIG_BT_SSP_ENABLED=n`) for legacy PIN pairing, and a GAP `PIN_REQ` handler that replies with the requesting host's BD_ADDR reversed. | The stack already implements HIDP + L2CAP (PSM 0x11/0x13) + auth, so this is the cheapest probe of Q1: if a real Wii connects + authenticates against the auto-generated SDP, we avoid hand-building raw SDP entirely. If it rejects it, fall back to raw L2CAP + the exact SDP record from `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator` (cloned locally for byte-exact bytes; WebFetch can't reproduce the ~463-byte blob). |
146	| 2026-06-12 | **Target the console-SYNC *bonding* flow, not the 1+2 temporary flow.** PIN handler returns the connecting host's (Wii's) BD_ADDR reversed (`param->pin_req.bda` byte-reversed). | Bonding (red SYNC button under the Wii's SD cover + controller in sync mode) is how a controller gets *persistently* registered, which is what a robot wants. The 1+2 flow is one-time/temporary and uses the controller's own address instead. Resolves Q2. |
147	| 2026-06-12 | **Build fauxmote as a parallel, independent proof-of-concept subproject; the fretboard GPIO-press path stays authoritative.** New top-level firmware subproject `firmware/fauxmote/`. | Device-side Wiimote *emulation* to a real Wii is rare/novel (host-side use is common), so de-risk it in isolation before touching marvin/fretboard/edge-ai. Nothing in the existing actuation path changes until fauxmote is proven. |
148	| 2026-06-12 | **Framework = ESP-IDF (v6.x; v6.0.1 installed), Bluedroid in Bluetooth-Classic-only mode (BLE disabled).** | Wiimote uses Bluetooth Classic HID; ESP-IDF exposes the BT-Classic HID-device API (`esp_hidd_api.h`), custom SDP records, BD_ADDR control, and raw L2CAP — all of which emulation needs. Arduino-ESP32's BT-Classic HID-device support is too thin for the custom SDP/descriptor the Wiimote requires. |
149	| 2026-06-12 | **Board = Adafruit ESP32 Feather V2 (product 5400); its *original* ESP32 is the load-bearing choice.** | The original ESP32 has a Bluetooth Classic (BR/EDR) radio. ESP32-S3/C3 are BLE-only and cannot emulate a Wiimote. Confirmed the product 5400 is the Feather V2 (not a QT Py S3). |
150	| 2026-06-12 | **marvin↔fauxmote command link is deferred; early phases use a local test command source.** | Lets the hard part (ESP32↔Wii Bluetooth emulation) be developed and validated standalone. The likely eventual link mirrors the fretboard 1-byte fret/strum bitmask over UART, but that's a later-session decision. |

```text
1	# marvin ↔ fauxmote command link
2	
3	> Protocol spec for the control link between **marvin** (SAM9X75 runtime brain) and
4	> **fauxmote** (ESP32 Wiimote/guitar emulator). marvin sends controller input;
5	> fauxmote reflects it to the real Wii. This is an alternative to the T1S
6	> `guitar` actuator node — fauxmote *becomes* the controller instead of pressing a
7	> real one.
8	>
9	> Companion docs: [`firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md`](../firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md),
10	> [`firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md`](../firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md), and the
11	> T1S bus link [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](t1s-podl-link.md) (the eventual second transport).
12	
13	**Protocol version:** 1. Both ends are compiled to a matching version for now
14	(no runtime negotiation); the version is reported in `STATUS` so a mismatch is
15	visible.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 1. Design goals
20	
21	1. **Low-latency gameplay control.** The hot path — frets, strum, whammy — is a
22	   single tiny fixed message fauxmote acts on immediately. No handshake, no ack,
23	   no per-message state machine.
24	2. **Absolute state, latest-wins.** Every input message carries the *complete
25	   current state* of its group, not deltas or events. Idempotent: a dropped or
26	   corrupt frame self-corrects on the next one. This matches both ends — marvin's
27	   existing 1-byte guitar bitmask is latest-wins, and fauxmote already streams the
28	   current state to the Wii every ~15 ms regardless of the command source.
29	3. **Transport-independent message layer.** The message bytes (§4) are identical
30	   over any physical layer. UART is the first transport (§3); 10BASE-T1S is the
31	   planned second (§6). Only the framing/binding changes.
32	4. **Fail safe.** If the command link goes quiet, fauxmote releases all inputs —
33	   a dropped link must never leave a note held.
34	
35	## 2. Layering
36	
37	```
38	  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
39	  │  L3  Message layer   TYPE + fixed payload     │  ← identical on every transport
40	  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
41	  │  L2  Framing layer   delimit + integrity      │  ← UART: SOF/LEN/CRC (§3.2)
42	  │                                               │     T1S: none (Ethernet FCS) (§6)
43	  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
44	  │  L1  Physical        UART now / T1S later      │
45	  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
46	```
47	
48	Both firmwares implement the message layer against a thin transport seam
49	(`send(type, payload, len)` / `on_message(type, payload, len)`); UART and T1S are
50	two implementations of that seam (§7).
51	
52	## 3. UART transport (transport #1)
53	
54	### 3.1 Physical
55	
56	| Parameter | Value |
57	|---|---|
58	| Baud | **1 000 000** (1 Mbaud), 8-N-1, no flow control |
59	| Wiring | 3 wires: marvin TX → fauxmote RX, fauxmote TX → marvin RX, common GND |
60	| marvin port | a spare FLEXCOM in USART mode (TBD at integration; the legacy fretboard UART is freed as that path moves to T1S) |
61	| fauxmote port | **UART1** on the Feather V2's broken-out RX=`GPIO7` / TX=`GPIO8` (the board's second hardware UART, `Serial1`) — **not** UART0, which is the USB-CDC console/CLI |
62	
63	Baud is generous on purpose: a 7-byte hot frame is ~70 µs on the wire, negligible
64	against the Wii's ~15 ms report period, so the link adds no meaningful latency.
65	Baud is a compile-time constant on both ends and may be lowered if wiring
66	reliability requires it.
67	
68	### 3.2 Framing
69	
70	Each message is wrapped in a frame:
71	
72	```
73	  ┌──────┬──────┬──────┬───────────────┬──────┐
74	  │ SOF  │ TYPE │ LEN  │  payload[LEN]  │ CRC8 │
75	  │ 0x7E │      │      │                │      │
76	  └──────┴──────┴──────┴───────────────┴──────┘
77	```
78	
79	- `SOF` = `0x7E` — start-of-frame marker.
80	- `TYPE` — message type (§4).
81	- `LEN` — payload length in bytes (0..255). Fixed per type in v1; carried anyway
82	  for extensibility and to bound the frame during resync.
83	- `payload` — `LEN` bytes (§5).
84	- `CRC8` — over `TYPE`, `LEN`, and the payload bytes (not `SOF`).
85	  Polynomial `0x07` (CRC-8/CCITT), init `0x00`, no reflection.
86	
87	Framing overhead is 4 bytes; a 3-byte `GUITAR` payload is 7 bytes on the wire.
88	
89	**Receiver rules:**
90	- Scan for `SOF`, then read `TYPE`/`LEN`, then `LEN` payload bytes, then `CRC8`.
91	- If the CRC fails, or `LEN` disagrees with the known length for `TYPE`, **discard
92	  and rescan** from the next `0x7E`. (A `0x7E` inside a payload that causes a false
93	  frame is rejected by the CRC and the receiver re-syncs on the real boundary.)
94	- `TYPE = 0x00` is never valid — treat as noise and rescan.
95	- No ack on any message; corruption self-heals on the next state frame.
96	
97	## 4. Message types
98	
99	| TYPE | Name | Dir | LEN | Status | Purpose |
100	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
101	| `0x01` | `GUITAR` | m→f | 3 | v1 | Hot gameplay input (frets/strum/whammy/aux). |
102	| `0x02` | `WIIMOTE` | m→f | 4 | v1 | Menu-nav input (core buttons, D-pad, analog stick). |
103	| `0x03` | `LINK_CMD` | m→f | 1 | v1 | Bluetooth link management (pair/stop/reconnect/unlink/ext). |
104	| `0x04` | `ACCEL` | m→f | 3 | planned | Wiimote accelerometer state (tilt → star power, motion). |
105	| `0x05` | `POINTER` | m→f | 3 | v1 | IR pointer position (bare-Wiimote menu nav). |
106	| `0x81` | `STATUS` | f→m | 4 | v1 | Link/connection/extension state + last-command result. |
107	
108	`0x00` reserved (invalid). `0x06`–`0x7F` reserved for future m→f; `0x82`–`0xFF`
109	for future f→m (telemetry). Each message updates one **independent slice** of the
110	latched controller state (§4.1) — new slices are added as new types without
111	touching existing ones.
112	
113	### 4.1 State model — independent slices, latched with timeout
114	
115	fauxmote holds a **single controller state** (buttons, whammy, stick, accelerometer,
116	IR pointer, extension bytes). Its report sender already assembles the Wii Bluetooth
117	report from that state every ~15 ms, independent of the command source.
118	
119	Each message type updates **one independent slice** of that state and nothing else —
120	`GUITAR` never touches the accel slice, `POINTER` never touches the frets, etc. So
121	the messages are fully independent: marvin sends whichever slices it needs, at
122	whatever rate each needs, in any order. fauxmote latches each slice and keeps
123	sending it to the Wii until a newer message for that slice replaces it.
124	
125	A **single link watchdog** (§6) guards the whole state: any control message
126	(`GUITAR`/`WIIMOTE`/`ACCEL`/`POINTER`) resets it. So long as fauxmote receives *any*
127	control message within the timeout, it holds all latched slices; if the link goes
128	fully quiet past the timeout, it reverts *all* slices to their safe defaults. This
129	is the core of the design — the wire protocol is a set of independent state-slice
130	updaters over one live link, not a single monolithic frame.
131	
132	## 5. Message payloads
133	
134	All fields are single bytes, so byte order is irrelevant. Bits are numbered
135	`bit0` = LSB. Reserved bits/bytes are sent `0` and ignored on receive.
136	
137	### 5.1 `GUITAR` (m→f, 3 bytes) — the hot path
138	
139	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| 0 | fret/strum mask | `bit0` Green, `bit1` Red, `bit2` Yellow, `bit3` Blue, `bit4` Orange, `bit5` Strum-Down, `bit6` Strum-Up, `bit7` reserved |
142	| 1 | whammy | raw 5-bit extension value `0..31`: rest ≈ `0x10`, fully pressed ≈ `0x1F` (upper bits 0) |
143	| 2 | aux | `bit0` Start (`+`), `bit1` Select (`−`), `bit2` Pedal, `bit3` Star-Power*, `bit4`–`7` reserved |
144	
145	Byte 0 is **bit-identical to marvin's existing guitar-node command bitmask** (the
146	[`T1SLink_SendToGuitar`](../firmware/marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.h) mask),
147	so marvin feeds the same computed mask to either actuation sink with no
148	translation.
149	
150	\* Star-Power is a semantic bit: fauxmote maps it to whatever mechanism activates
151	SP in-game (GH3 uses a Wiimote tilt, not a button — driven via the `ACCEL` slice,
152	§5.5). **Not implemented in fauxmote yet** (the emulator streams a fixed level
153	accel); a no-op until the `ACCEL` slice goes live.
154	
155	### 5.2 `WIIMOTE` (m→f, 4 bytes) — menu navigation
156	
157	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
158	|---|---|---|
159	| 0 | core buttons | `bit0` A, `bit1` B, `bit2` One, `bit3` Two, `bit4` Plus, `bit5` Minus, `bit6` Home, `bit7` reserved |
160	| 1 | D-pad | `bit0` Up, `bit1` Down, `bit2` Left, `bit3` Right, `bit4`–`7` reserved |
161	| 2 | stick X | `0..63`, center `32` (the guitar extension's 6-bit analog stick) |
162	| 3 | stick Y | `0..63`, center `32` |
163	
164	The analog stick is the guitar-mode Home-menu control (the IR pointer is
165	physically blocked when the Wiimote is seated in the guitar — see the fauxmote
166	journal). Bare-Wiimote menu nav uses the separate `POINTER` slice (§5.6).
167	
168	### 5.5 `ACCEL` (m→f, 3 bytes) — *planned*
169	
170	Wiimote accelerometer state, the same slice used to synthesize star-power tilt in
171	GH3 and general motion input. Independent of `GUITAR`.
172	
173	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
174	|---|---|---|
175	| 0 | accel X | `0..255`, center `128` (mapped to the Wiimote's accel range) |
176	| 1 | accel Y | `0..255`, center `128` |
177	| 2 | accel Z | `0..255`, center `128` (gravity ~+1 g at rest) |
178	
179	Default when the slice is stale/absent: **level** (all `128`, i.e. Z at +1 g). Not
180	consumed by fauxmote yet — the emulator currently streams a fixed level accel;
181	`ACCEL` goes live when fauxmote drives the accel field from this slice (which also
182	makes the `GUITAR` aux star-power bit meaningful). A finer 10-bit encoding can be
183	added later without changing the type.
184	
185	### 5.6 `POINTER` (m→f, 3 bytes)
186	
187	IR pointer position, for bare-Wiimote menu navigation. marvin sends it via
188	`Fauxmote_SendPointer(x, y, visible)` (latched, on-change); fauxmote applies it
189	through `Wiimote_SetPointer`/`ClearPointer`. Independent of `WIIMOTE`. Moot while
190	the Wiimote is seated in the guitar (camera blocked) — use the analog stick there.
191	
192	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
193	|---|---|---|
194	| 0 | x | `0..255` → `0..1`, `0` = left edge |
195	| 1 | y | `0..255` → `0..1`, `0` = top edge |
196	| 2 | flags | `bit0` `MF_PTR_VISIBLE` (`0` = pointer off / off-screen), `bit1`–`7` reserved |
197	
198	Console: `fauxmote pointer <x> <y>` / `fauxmote pointer off`.
199	
200	Default when the slice is stale/absent: **off** (pointer off-screen).
201	
202	### 5.3 `LINK_CMD` (m→f, 1 byte) — Bluetooth link management
203	
204	Mirrors the fauxmote CLI so marvin owns the whole link lifecycle. Fire-and-forget;
205	the result is reflected in the next `STATUS`.
206	
207	| Byte | Field | Values |
208	|---|---|---|
209	| 0 | opcode | `0x01` PAIR (enter sync/pairing) · `0x02` STOP (leave pairing) · `0x03` RECONNECT · `0x04` UNLINK (erase bond) · `0x05` EXT_ATTACH · `0x06` EXT_DETACH · `0x07` STATUS_REQ (send a `STATUS` now) |
210	
211	### 5.4 `STATUS` (f→m, 4 bytes) — the uplink
212	
213	Sent on any state change **and** as a heartbeat (~2 Hz) so marvin can tell the link
214	is alive and gate/annotate commands.
215	
216	| Byte | Field | Encoding |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| 0 | flags | `bit0` discoverable, `bit1` connected (HID data channel), `bit2` assigned (Wii gave a player slot), `bit3` ext-attached, `bit4` pairing-active, `bit5` bonded (bond in NVS), `bit6`–`7` reserved. fauxmote sets `bit0` and `bit4` **together** — discoverable and pairing-active are the same state in the current code |
219	| 1 | player_slot | `0` = none, else `1..4` |
220	| 2 | report_mode | the Wii's last-requested report ID (e.g. `0x37`); defaults to `0x30` (core buttons) before the Wii sets a mode, never `0` |
221	| 3 | last_result | result of the most recent `LINK_CMD`: `0` = ok/idle, nonzero = error code |
222	
223	## 6. Semantics & timing
224	
225	- **Absolute / latest-wins, per slice.** Every input message carries the full
226	  current state of *its slice* (§4.1). fauxmote latches the most recent message per
227	  slice and reflects all latched slices in its next Wii report. No history, no
228	  ordering requirement beyond last-writer-wins within a slice.
229	- **Send policy (marvin).** Send a slice on any change; additionally resend it at a
230	  floor rate (~10 Hz) so a dropped frame self-corrects. Bursting faster than the Wii
231	  report cadence (~15 ms) is wasted. marvin sends only the slices it needs —
232	  `GUITAR` continuously during gameplay, `WIIMOTE`/`POINTER` only while navigating.
233	- **Fail-safe (fauxmote), one watchdog.** A single **link timeout** (200 ms
234	  default) is reset by *any* control message. While it holds, all latched slices
235	  stay in effect. On expiry (the link has gone fully quiet) fauxmote reverts *all*
236	  slices to their safe defaults at once — `GUITAR` frets/strum released + whammy
237	  rest (≈ `0x10`), `WIIMOTE` buttons released / stick centered, `ACCEL` level, `POINTER`
238	  off. A dead link never holds a note. (marvin's ~10 Hz refresh of at least one
239	  slice keeps the watchdog alive during normal play.)
240	- **`STATUS` cadence (fauxmote).** On every state change, plus a ~500 ms heartbeat,
241	  plus immediately on `STATUS_REQ`.
242	- **`LINK_CMD`** is fire-and-forget; marvin reads the outcome in the following
243	  `STATUS`.
244	
245	## 7. Implementation seam (both ends)
246	
247	Keep the message layer transport-agnostic so the T1S move (§8) is a transport swap,
248	not a rewrite.
249	
250	**fauxmote** — `main/marvin_link.c` (implemented 2026-07-02):
251	- Owns the second UART, the §3.2 framing/CRC, and message parse/dispatch (FreeRTOS
252	  task); started at boot via `MarvinLink_Start()`.
253	- On `GUITAR`/`WIIMOTE`/`LINK_CMD`, calls the **same module APIs the CLI uses**
254	  (`Wiimote_SetButton`, `Guitar_SetWhammy`, `Wiimote_SetPointer`,
255	  `Fauxmote_EnterPairing`/`StopPairing`/`Reconnect`/`Unlink`, `Wiimote_SetExtension`),
256	  so the link is a second front-end over existing logic — no behavior duplicated.
257	- Emits `STATUS` from the existing `Wiimote_Is*` / `Fauxmote_*` state.
258	- The CLI stays for manual bring-up/debug.
259	
260	**marvin** — `net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.c` (implemented 2026-07-02):
261	- Owns the **FLEXCOM1 USART (PA28/PA29)** — the fretboard UART-transport pins, free
262	  while the guitar node rides T1S — and the framing. Exposes
263	  `Fauxmote_SendGuitar(mask, whammy, aux)` / `SendGuitarMask(mask)`,
264	  `Fauxmote_SendNav(...)`, `Fauxmote_SendCmd(op)`, and `Fauxmote_GetStatus(...)`.
265	- A TX task re-sends the latched `GUITAR` slice on change (low latency) and at a
266	  50 ms floor; an RX task parses the `STATUS` uplink.
267	- **Mirror-to-both** (not a switched sink): `FretboardLink_Send()` — the one choke
268	  point both producers (timing pipeline + `manual_control`) call — also calls
269	  `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask()`, so the T1S guitar node and fauxmote move in lock-step.
270	  `GUITAR` byte 0 == the T1S 7-bit mask. Compile-guarded to the T1S guitar build
271	  (fauxmote owns FLEXCOM1, mutually exclusive with a `TRANSPORT=UART` guitar).
272	
273	## 8. T1S transport (transport #2, future)
274	
275	When fauxmote (or a successor node) joins the T1S bus, the **message layer (§4–§5)
276	travels unchanged as the payload of a T1S Ethernet frame**:
277	
278	- The UART framing layer (§3.2) is dropped — the Ethernet frame provides delimiting
279	  and an FCS; `TYPE` + payload become the frame payload.
280	- Addressed marvin ↔ fauxmote-node like the other T1S nodes (see
281	  [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](t1s-podl-link.md) §7 for the addressing/ethertype scheme).
282	- Only the transport seam (§7) changes; message handling and semantics are identical.
283	
284	**Caveat:** the current ESP32 Feather has no 10BASE-T1S MAC-PHY, so this transport
285	is hardware-dependent and genuinely future work; UART is the working link.
286	
287	## 9. Open questions
288	
289	- ~~Exact marvin FLEXCOM instance + pins~~ **settled 2026-07-02:** marvin =
290	  **FLEXCOM1 / PA28 (TX) / PA29 (RX)** (the fretboard UART-transport pins, free while
291	  the guitar rides T1S); fauxmote = UART1 on Feather RX=`GPIO7` / TX=`GPIO8`. Wiring:
292	  marvin PA28 → ESP `GPIO7`, ESP `GPIO8` → marvin PA29, common GND.
293	- When to make the planned `ACCEL` slice live in fauxmote (drive the Wiimote accel
294	  field from it) — this is what makes GH3 star power (`GUITAR` aux `bit3`) work.
295	- Whether `ACCEL` needs finer than 8-bit-per-axis for smooth tilt; 10-bit can be
296	  added under the same type.
297	- Runtime version negotiation (a `HELLO` exchange) if the two ends ever ship
298	  independently; unnecessary while both are built from this repo.

25	
26	static void recompute_and_send(void)
27	{
28	    if (!s_enabled) { return; }
29	    uint8_t mask = (uint8_t)(s_fret_mask | s_strum_mask);
30	    FretboardLink_Send(mask, (uint8_t)PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_MANUAL);

35	}

40	}

42	void ManualControl_SetEnabled(bool enabled)
43	{
44	    if (enabled == s_enabled) { return; }
45	
46	    if (enabled)
47	    {
48	        /* Gate the pipeline before we own the wire so the next pipeline
49	         * frame can't race a stale mask onto the link between our zero
50	         * and our enable flip. */
51	        TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false);
52	        s_fret_mask = 0u;
53	        s_strum_mask = 0u;
54	        s_enabled = true;
55	        FretboardLink_Send(0u, (uint8_t)PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_MANUAL);
56	        LOG_INFO("MC: manual mode on\r\n");
57	    }
58	    else
59	    {
60	        /* Release while we still own the wire, then hand back. The
61	         * pipeline's next advance() (≤ TP_TICK_MS = 5 ms) republishes
62	         * its own correct mask. */
63	        s_enabled = false;
64	        s_fret_mask = 0u;
65	        s_strum_mask = 0u;
66	        FretboardLink_Send(0u, (uint8_t)PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_MANUAL);
67	        TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(true);
68	        LOG_INFO("MC: manual mode off\r\n");
69	    }
70	}
71	
72	void ManualControl_SetFret(fret_t fret, bool pressed)
73	{
74	    if ((unsigned)fret >= FRET_COUNT) { return; }
75	    uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[fret];
76	    if (pressed) { s_fret_mask |= bit; }
77	    else         { s_fret_mask &= (uint8_t)~bit; }
78	    recompute_and_send();
79	}
80	
81	void ManualControl_SetStrum(bool down, bool pressed)
82	{
83	    uint8_t bit = down ? TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN : TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP;
84	    if (pressed) { s_strum_mask |= bit; }
85	    else         { s_strum_mask &= (uint8_t)~bit; }
86	    recompute_and_send();

38:**2026-07-07 — Wiimotes screen is now a nav-selectable base view; nav widget rename sync.** An MGS regen renamed the navigation widgets (dropped the `_0` suffix; `BUTTON_NAV_HAMBURGER` → `BUTTON_DASHBOARD_TITLEBAR_NAVIGATION`), gave the wiimotes screen proper names (`Marvin_panel_Marvin` → `Marvin_PANEL_WIIMOTES`, + `PANEL_WIIMOTES_*`/`BUTTON_WIIMOTES_*`), and added a **Wiimotes** nav entry + a titlebar hamburger on the wiimotes screen. Updated code to match and wired the entry.
39:- **Base-view swap (new compositor verb, first real use):** `UiManager_ShowDashboard()`/`UiManager_ShowWiimotes()` swap the BASE hw layer between `CANVAS_DASH` (layer 0) and `CANVAS_WIIMOTES` (layer 4). The outgoing canvas is **hidden first** (`gfxcSetLayer` requires the canvas inactive, and an active canvas drives its layer — two on BASE would fight), then the incoming one is bound. Showing wiimotes hides live video (HEO + OVR1 frame); returning restores it via `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()`. Mirrors the song-select open/close video handling.
40:- **Picking across a swap:** Legato picks across *all* attached layers regardless of canvas visibility, so the hidden view's panel must be gated off or it still intercepts touches. `UiManager_SetBaseViewPickable(on)` routes to the active view (`ScreenWiimotes_SetInput` / `UiManager_SetDashboardPickable`). The nav drawer now gates the **active base view** (was dashboard-only) — and because wiimotes is layer 4 (above the drawer's layer 1), gating it off is also what lets the open drawer receive touches over the wiimotes view.
41:- **Both titlebar hamburgers** (dashboard layer 0, wiimotes layer 4) wire to the same drawer toggle; the wiimotes one only picks while its view is shown (its subtree is gated otherwise).
42:- **Wiimotes fret buttons are inputs, not indicators (decided w/ Greg):** the wiimotes screen is for manual / override control, so its `BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_FRET_*` are *not* fed by the dashboard feed — they'll drive manual actuation, not mirror activity. Files: `ui/screens/navigation/screen_navigation.c`, `ui/screens/wiimotes/screen_wiimotes.{c,h}`, `ui/ui_manager.{c,h}`. No MCC/Legato hand-edits (MGS regen staged separately). **Pending Greg's MPLAB build + hardware validation** (nav → Wiimotes shows the screen; its hamburger opens the drawer; Dashboard returns; video returns with the dashboard; touch routes correctly in both views and with the drawer open).
124:**2026-07-02 — fauxmote command link (marvin TX side): mirror the gameplay mask to the ESP32 Wiimote over FLEXCOM1.** New `net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.{c,h}` transmits controller input to the fauxmote ESP32 over the **FLEXCOM1 USART (PA28/PA29)** — the fretboard UART-transport pins, which are **free while the guitar node rides T1S** (the current build, `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT=1`). Wire protocol is the shared `net/fauxmote/mf_proto.h` (byte-for-byte identical to `firmware/fauxmote/main/mf_proto.h`): `SOF/TYPE/LEN/CRC8` framing, `GUITAR`/`WIIMOTE`/`LINK_CMD` out + `STATUS` in. A TX task re-sends the latched `GUITAR` slice on change (low latency, via a notify) and at a 50 ms floor (self-heals dropped frames + feeds fauxmote's 200 ms watchdog); an RX task parses the `STATUS` uplink. **Routing = mirror-to-both:** `FretboardLink_Send()` (the single choke point both producers — timing pipeline + manual_control — already call) now also calls `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask(mask)`, so every gameplay mask drives the T1S guitar node **and** fauxmote in lock-step (`GUITAR` byte 0 == the T1S 7-bit mask). Init in `App_StartServices` (guarded to the T1S build; before the producers). `SerialSetup` bumps FLEXCOM1 to the link's 1 Mbaud at init (MCC default was 500000 for the guitar UART). New `fauxmote` console command drives it for bring-up (`status`/`pair`/`stop`/`reconnect`/`unlink`/`ext`/`btn <mask>`). **Constraint:** owns FLEXCOM1, so it's mutually exclusive with a `TRANSPORT=UART` guitar build (compile-guarded). **Code-complete; pending MPLAB build + on-hardware bring-up** with the ESP32 wired (marvin TX PA28→ESP RX GPIO7, ESP TX GPIO8→marvin RX PA29, common GND). Protocol spec: [`../../../docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md`](../../../docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md).
195:| 2026-07-02 | **fauxmote link on marvin uses FLEXCOM1 (PA28/PA29) and mirrors the gameplay mask to both sinks.** New `net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.c` reuses the fretboard UART-transport peripheral (free while the guitar rides T1S); `FretboardLink_Send()` taps `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask()` so the T1S guitar node and the ESP32 Wiimote move in lock-step. Shared `mf_proto.h` (byte-identical both sides); 1 Mbaud via `SerialSetup`. Compile-guarded to the T1S build (owns FLEXCOM1). | Zero MCC work — FLEXCOM1's USART PLIB already exists and is idle in the T1S build, so no new peripheral/pin generation. "Mirror to both" (Greg's call) keeps the real guitar and the Wii driven by the one existing choke point without a runtime multi-sink layer, and matches the spec's bit-identical `GUITAR` byte 0 == T1S mask. Latched-state TX task with a 50 ms floor gives low-latency-on-change plus dropped-frame self-heal and keeps fauxmote's watchdog fed. |

```text
#ifndef UI_WIDGET_BUTTON_AA_H
#define UI_WIDGET_BUTTON_AA_H

#include "gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* House default corner radius, shared so AA'd buttons look consistent. The AA path
 * supports any radius (coverage is computed analytically — see ui/gfx/aa_corners),
 * so this is just a convenient default, not a constraint. */
#define BUTTON_AA_RADIUS  12u

/* Anti-aliased rounded corners for a button. The classic skin draws rounded
 * corners (and any LINE border) with hard, stepped edges; calling this re-points
 * the button's vtable at a copy whose paint smooths the corner boxes after the
 * normal draw — backdrop → border → fill, at whatever cornerRadius the button has.
 * Set the radius (and border) first. Safe to call once per button after it is
 * constructed. */
void ButtonAA_Enable(leButtonWidget* btn);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* UI_WIDGET_BUTTON_AA_H */

I've reviewed the staged diff and traced the full wiring path. Here's what I found before we implement.

## Review of the staged files

All 11 staged files are **MGS/Legato-generated** (under `config/default/`), which per the project rules I won't hand-edit — the changes came out of the Legato designer and are correct to commit as-is. What the regen did:

**In [le_gen_screen_Marvin.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Marvin.h) / `.c`:** promoted a batch of anonymous `leWidget*`/label placeholders into properly-named `leButtonWidget*` handles. New named buttons:

- **Guitar slice** (children of `PANEL_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_GUITAR_EXTENSION`): `STRUM_UP`, `STRUM_DOWN`, `GUITAR_PLUS`, `GUITAR_MINUS` — joining the existing `FRET_{GREEN,RED,YELLOW,BLUE,ORANGE}`.
- **Wiimote nav slice**: `UP`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `DOWN`, `HOME`, `A`, `B`, `ONE`, `TWO`.

The old label/icon sub-widgets were folded into the buttons (strum buttons now carry the up/down arrow as pressed/released image + string). Font/stringtable/assets deltas are the fallout of removing those standalone labels. All consistent — nothing off in the generated code.

**Two things the regen did *not* name**, so they have no code handle to wire yet:
- `Marvin_panel_WhammySlider_1` — still an anonymous `leWidget*` panel (not an interactive slider).
- `Marvin_panel_TiltControl_1` — same.

So whammy and tilt can't be hooked up this pass unless you rename/convert them in MGS. The momentary buttons above are ready to wire.

## The wiring path is all in place

The transmit side already exists — [fauxmote_link.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.h) exposes `Fauxmote_SendGuitar(mask, whammy, aux)`, `Fauxmote_SendNav(core, dpad, stick_x, stick_y)`, and `Fauxmote_SendCmd(op)`, with the bit constants in [mf_proto.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/net/fauxmote/mf_proto.h) matching the button set exactly. The pattern for runtime-registering press/release callbacks + `ButtonAA_Enable` is established in [screen_navigation.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/screens/navigation/screen_navigation.c). So this is a focused new module (`screen_wiimotes.c` currently wires none of these buttons).

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 17:42:17Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should the on-screen guitar buttons (frets/strum/±) drive actuation?**

Options:
- **Direct to fauxmote** - Buttons call Fauxmote_SendGuitar() directly — drives only the ESP32 Wiimote, independent of the real T1S guitar node. Simplest; matches 'hook up to fauxmote' literally. Note: fights the timing pipeline's mirrored masks if a song is playing.
- **Through ManualControl** - Route frets/strum through ManualControl (gates the timing pipeline, mirrors to BOTH the real T1S guitar and fauxmote). Reuses existing manual-mode logic; needs manual mode enabled. ±/nav still go direct since ManualControl has no path for them.

**How should nav/core buttons (D-pad, A/B/1/2, Home, ±) behave on touch?**

Options:
- **Momentary (hold)** - Pressed on touch-down, released on touch-up — held only while the finger is down. Natural for Legato press/release events; matches how a real button feels.
- **Latching (toggle)** - Each tap toggles the button on/off, stays until tapped again. Useful for one-finger operation but unusual for D-pad/Home.


**Answer:** wiimotes screen should send directly to fauxmote. manual control from wiimotes screen takes priority and blocks any other fauxmote commands , Momentary (hold)
</details></tool-use>

## Plan

**1. `net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.{h,c}` — priority gate.** Add `Fauxmote_SetOverride(bool)`. While engaged, `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask()` (the gameplay-mirror hook the timing pipeline calls via `FretboardLink_Send`) becomes a no-op, so the wiimotes screen's direct `Fauxmote_SendGuitar`/`SendNav` own the fauxmote state. The real T1S guitar keeps playing; only fauxmote's feed is commandeered.

**2. `ui/screens/wiimotes/screen_wiimotes.{c,h}` — button wiring.** Momentary press/release handlers for the newly-named buttons, keyed by a widget→(field, bit) table:
- Guitar mask: `FRET_{GREEN,RED,YELLOW,BLUE,ORANGE}`, `STRUM_UP/DOWN` → `Fauxmote_SendGuitar(mask, MF_WHAMMY_REST, aux)`
- Guitar aux: `GUITAR_PLUS/MINUS` → `MF_AUX_PLUS/MINUS`
- Nav core: `A,B,ONE,TWO,HOME`; nav dpad: `UP,DOWN,LEFT,RIGHT` → `Fauxmote_SendNav(core, dpad, center, center)`

New `ScreenWiimotes_SetShown(bool)`: on show → engage override + zero state; on hide → send neutral guitar/nav then release override (never leave a note held). Distinct from `SetInput` (which the drawer modal reuses).

**3. `ui/ui_manager.c`** — call `ScreenWiimotes_SetShown(true/false)` from `ShowWiimotes`/`ShowDashboard`.

Whammy slider + tilt are left out — MGS didn't give them named/interactive handles yet.

#include "ui/screens/wiimotes/screen_wiimotes.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

#include "ui/ui_manager.h"   /* CANVAS_WIIMOTES, BASE_W, BASE_H */

#include "gfx/canvas/gfx_canvas_api.h"
#include "gfx/legato/legato.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Marvin.h"   /* wiimotes widgets */

#include "net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.h"
#include "net/fauxmote/mf_proto.h"

/* Wiimotes surface, non-cached so the 2D engine and LCDC DMA read CPU-rendered
 * pixels coherently; 32-byte aligned. RGB565 to match the layer's color mode. */
#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))

static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb[BASE_W * BASE_H];

/* Manual-override control state, sent directly to fauxmote. Frets/strum/± form the
 * GUITAR slice (whammy fixed at rest — no slider handle yet); D-pad + core buttons
 * form the WIIMOTE nav slice (stick centered). Momentary: a button holds its bit
 * only while pressed. While this screen is shown it owns fauxmote (override on), so
 * the gameplay mirror can't fight these values. */
static uint8_t s_g_mask;    /* MF_G_*  */
static uint8_t s_g_aux;     /* MF_AUX_* */
static uint8_t s_nav_core;  /* MF_W_A/B/ONE/TWO/HOME */
static uint8_t s_nav_dpad;  /* MF_W_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT */

/* Which slice/field a control button drives. */
typedef enum { FLD_GMASK, FLD_GAUX, FLD_NCORE, FLD_NDPAD } ctrl_field_t;

typedef struct
{
    leButtonWidget **slot;   /* address of the MGS-assigned widget global */
    ctrl_field_t     field;
    uint8_t          bit;
} ctrl_map_t;

/* Every control button on the screen, mapped to its fauxmote bit. The widget
 * globals are assigned by screenShow_Marvin, so the table holds their addresses and
 * dereferences at dispatch time. */
static const ctrl_map_t s_ctrls[] =
{
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_FRET_GREEN,  FLD_GMASK, MF_G_GREEN      },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_FRET_RED,    FLD_GMASK, MF_G_RED        },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_FRET_YELLOW, FLD_GMASK, MF_G_YELLOW     },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_FRET_BLUE,   FLD_GMASK, MF_G_BLUE       },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_FRET_ORANGE, FLD_GMASK, MF_G_ORANGE     },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_STRUM_UP,    FLD_GMASK, MF_G_STRUM_UP   },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_STRUM_DOWN,  FLD_GMASK, MF_G_STRUM_DOWN },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_GUITAR_PLUS,  FLD_GAUX, MF_AUX_PLUS     },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_GUITAR_MINUS, FLD_GAUX, MF_AUX_MINUS    },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_A,    FLD_NCORE, MF_W_A    },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_B,    FLD_NCORE, MF_W_B    },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_ONE,  FLD_NCORE, MF_W_ONE  },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_TWO,  FLD_NCORE, MF_W_TWO  },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_HOME, FLD_NCORE, MF_W_HOME },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_UP,    FLD_NDPAD, MF_W_UP    },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_DOWN,  FLD_NDPAD, MF_W_DOWN  },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_LEFT,  FLD_NDPAD, MF_W_LEFT  },
    { &Marvin_BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_RIGHT, FLD_NDPAD, MF_W_RIGHT },
};

#define CTRL_COUNT  (sizeof(s_ctrls) / sizeof(s_ctrls[0]))

static void send_guitar(void)
{
    Fauxmote_SendGuitar(s_g_mask, MF_WHAMMY_REST, s_g_aux);
}

static void send_nav(void)
{
    Fauxmote_SendNav(s_nav_core, s_nav_dpad, MF_STICK_CENTER, MF_STICK_CENTER);
}

/* Apply a press/release to whichever field the button owns, then push that slice. */
static void control_apply(const ctrl_map_t *c, bool pressed)
{
    uint8_t *field;

    switch (c->field)
    {
        case FLD_GMASK: field = &s_g_mask;   break;
        case FLD_GAUX:  field = &s_g_aux;    break;
        case FLD_NCORE: field = &s_nav_core; break;
        default:        field = &s_nav_dpad; break;
    }

    if (pressed) { *field |= c->bit; }
    else         { *field &= (uint8_t)~c->bit; }

    if (c->field == FLD_GMASK || c->field == FLD_GAUX) { send_guitar(); }
    else                                               { send_nav(); }
}

static void control_dispatch(leButtonWidget *btn, bool pressed)
{
    unsigned int i;

    for (i = 0u; i < CTRL_COUNT; i++)
    {
        if (*s_ctrls[i].slot == btn) { control_apply(&s_ctrls[i], pressed); return; }
    }
}

static void control_on_press(leButtonWidget *btn)   { control_dispatch(btn, true); }
static void control_on_release(leButtonWidget *btn) { control_dispatch(btn, false); }

/* Register momentary press/release on every control button (runtime-wired here — the
 * MGS screen wires no button events). */
static void controls_init(void)
{
    unsigned int i;

    for (i = 0u; i < CTRL_COUNT; i++)
    {
        leButtonWidget *b = *s_ctrls[i].slot;
        b->fn->setPressedEventCallback(b, control_on_press);
        b->fn->setReleasedEventCallback(b, control_on_release);
    }
}

void ScreenWiimotes_InitSurface(void)
{
    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_WIIMOTES, BASE_W, BASE_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb);
}

void ScreenWiimotes_Setup(void)
{
    /* Full-screen at the origin. The root is on Legato layer 4 (built by MGS); the
     * canvas window positions that layer's pixels on the display. */
    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_WIIMOTES, 0, 0);
    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_WIIMOTES, BASE_W, BASE_H);

    controls_init();

    /* Start not shown → gate out of picking (see ScreenWiimotes_SetInput). */
    ScreenWiimotes_SetInput(false);
}

/* Gate the screen's whole subtree in/out of picking. Legato picks across every
 * attached layer top-to-bottom regardless of canvas visibility, so while this
 * screen isn't the shown base view its background panel would otherwise swallow
 * touches meant for the view beneath it. Clearing LE_WIDGET_ENABLED on the
 * background panel gates the subtree without repainting (leUtils_PickFromWidget
 * descends only into ENABLED children; the renderer never reads the flag) — the
 * same mechanism ui_manager uses for the closed song-select overlays. ui_manager
 * drives this on base-view show/hide and drawer-modal open/close. */
void ScreenWiimotes_SetInput(bool on)
{
    if (on) { Marvin_PANEL_WIIMOTES->flags |=  LE_WIDGET_ENABLED; }
    else    { Marvin_PANEL_WIIMOTES->flags &= ~LE_WIDGET_ENABLED; }
}

/* Take/relinquish the fauxmote link as this base view is shown/hidden. While shown
 * the screen owns the GUITAR slice (override blocks the gameplay mirror) and drives
 * fauxmote directly from its buttons. On hide, release every input to safe defaults
 * *before* dropping the override so a dead touch never leaves a note held, then hand
 * fauxmote back to the gameplay mirror. */
void ScreenWiimotes_SetShown(bool shown)
{
    s_g_mask   = 0u;
    s_g_aux    = 0u;
    s_nav_core = 0u;
    s_nav_dpad = 0u;

    if (shown)
    {
        Fauxmote_SetOverride(true);
        send_guitar();
        send_nav();
    }
    else
    {
        send_guitar();
        send_nav();
        Fauxmote_SetOverride(false);
    }
}

1	# marvin — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.
4	
5	---
6	
7	**2026-07-10 — streak: cleaned the training set + units-wrap tens carry (host + regen header; pending build).** Two linked changes after Greg reviewed the corpus. (1) **Audit:** the auto-selected units exemplars had let mid-roll samples in (a rolling wheel half-transitioned reads as a digit and smears the template); removed them / relabelled the rolling ones to units-`x`, corpus 76→65. Future policy: a digit is usable only if identical across neighbouring frames. (2) **Units-wrap tens carry** (`gp_streak_track`): cleaner data made units-9 read better, exposing the tens carry lag (49→40→50). Now a confident units read that drops ≥`GP_STREAK_WRAP_MIN`(5) steps the current (debounced) tens by one — applying the carry the instant the ones rolls (49→50). Works off the debounced digits and fires only on a genuine wrap, so it can't re-inflate a stale value: a wrong-high tens corrected downward stays corrected (guards the "stuck 30-high, can't recover" failure Greg flagged; regression-tested). Capture: carry-lag dips 30→0, anchors exact, 76 tests. Only `game/gameplay_score.c` (tracker) + regenerated `gameplay_metadata.h` (cleaned banks + WRAP_MIN) change. **Pending Greg's MPLAB build.** See gameplay journal 2026-07-10.
8	
9	**2026-07-10 — score + streak readers rewritten to integer math; fixed a coverage out-of-bounds bug (pending build).** Converted the shared coverage pipeline (luma → ink threshold → grid resize → per-cell coverage) in `gameplay_score.c` to pure integer so the firmware reproduces the host prototype **bit-for-bit**. This directly cuts hardware misreads: the device was extracting coverage in float32 while templates were built/validated in float64 (plus different rounding modes), so its reads diverged from what was validated. Now luma = `B*29+G*150+R*77` (no /256), ink threshold = rational `GP_{SCORE,STREAK}_INK_NUM/DEN` of the min..max range (`DEN*(luma-lo) ≷ NUM*(hi-lo)`), integer `gp_edge`, integer coverage; no float in the readers (ARM926 has no FPU). **Also fixed a real OOB bug**: when an ink bbox is smaller than the glyph grid, the last cell's block ran past the bbox and read the unused tail of the scratch buffer (stale data) → wrong coverage on short glyphs; clamped `yb→rh`/`xb→rw` to match the host (numpy) slice. Cross-check is now strict bit-exact (presence + every digit + every confidence flag). Digit banks in `gameplay_metadata.h` rebuilt with integer coverage. Files: `game/gameplay_score.c`, `game/gameplay_metadata.h` (regen). The multiplier (colour counts) was already integer. **Pending Greg's MPLAB build.** See gameplay journal 2026-07-10.
10	
11	**2026-07-10 — dashboard streak label wasn't clearing at song start / after a miss (fixed).** The streak label kept showing the pre-reset count. `ScreenDashboard_ApplyStreak` set an *empty* string for streak 0, and `lestring_set_utf8("")` doesn't repaint/clear the prior glyphs (the score/status labels never hit this — they always render non-empty). Fix: always render the number, so 0 shows "0" and repaints. Both reset paths already posted 0 (song start `run()` → `PostStreak(0)`; miss → tracker resets to 0 when the odometer isn't locked); only the label paint was the bug. File: `ui/screens/dashboard/screen_dashboard.c`. **Pending Greg's MPLAB build.**
12	
13	**2026-07-10 — streak reader: grew the units corpus to fix 9/0/6 detection (host-only; regenerated header).** The dark-on-light units wheel has a fat distance tail, so a correct digit from an under-sampled template exceeded the confidence gate and was dropped — most visibly units-9 (4 exemplars → real 9s at dist ~12300 > gate 9500, "rarely detects 9"). Mined the 6549-frame capture for 30 more **units-only** exemplars (10 each of 9/0/6, `streak__xx<u>__cap…` so they feed only the dark-on-light bank and leave the white-on-dark bank the clean original). units-9 median distance 12300→~5700 (clears the gate); capture confident units-9 reads 0→256; in-sample 154/154; tracker unchanged (0 big jumps, max 304, anchors exact). Only `gameplay_metadata.h` (regenerated digit banks) changes on the firmware side — no logic change. See gameplay journal 2026-07-10. **Pending Greg's MPLAB build.**
14	
15	**2026-07-10 — gameplay_engine: streak tracker debounce + plausibility clamp (pending build).** Fixed a reported streak **lock** and two failures it surfaced, all in `gp_streak_track` (host-proven, see gameplay journal 2026-07-10). The old monotonic forward window couldn't represent a value below `last`, so a tens misread locked the value high (11x→14x…); "confident read trumps" fixed that but unmasked a systematic **tens 0↔8 flicker** (the slashed zero's top loop closes under aliasing → reads 8 confidently, 100↔180) and a **carry-roll 900 blip** (mid-roll hundreds reads 9 for ~2 frames at 99→100). Fix, both symmetric so they never lock: **per-place debounce** (`GP_STREAK_DEBOUNCE {2,2,1}` — a changed digit commits after N consecutive confident reads; slow wheels 2, units immediate) + a **plausibility clamp** (`GP_STREAK_MAX_STEP 50` — reject a committed per-frame value jump a streak can't make; seed bypasses it). `gp_streak_state_t` gains `pend[3]`/`pend_n[3]`. Over the capture: 0 implausible jumps, max 304, anchors exact; host suite 74. Still open: units-9 detection (needs more units exemplars — corpus-growth pass next). Files: `game/gameplay_score.{c,h}`, `game/gameplay_metadata.h` (regen). **Pending Greg's MPLAB build.**
16	
17	**2026-07-10 — gameplay_engine: note-streak reader (odometer OCR + confident-read tracker) → dashboard STREAK label (pending build).** Last scoring-block value after score + multiplier. The streak is a 3-tumbler odometer (note icon + hundreds/tens/units) that only appears at ~25+ and whose wheels *roll* — the units constantly, tens/hundreds at carries — so any frame can show unreadable wheels. Proven host-side (`tools/gameplay`, see its journal 2026-07-10) then ported.
18	- **Stateless read (`gp_read_streak`, `gameplay_score.c`, pure/cross-checked).** **Presence = the odometer is *locked at its final position*, detected from the note icon — not the digits** (Greg): the counter slides in from the bottom, overshoots, and bounces down to settle (`score-0335.png` = reference locked frame), and mid-slide the cells are misaligned → garbage. The fixed gold note glyph is a position fiducial — its coverage matches the locked template (L1 < `GP_STREAK_NOTE_MAX_SAD`) only when settled, cleanly rejecting both absent and slide/overshoot frames. When locked, three fixed cells (units dark-on-light, tens/hundreds white-on-dark) → 16×10 coverage → integer-L1 argmin over a **per-polarity 0-9 bank**; a wheel failing the gate is flagged unreadable. Fills `{present, digit[3], known[3]}`. Data frozen into `gameplay_metadata.h` (`GP_STREAK_*`: note template + two digit banks + ROIs + thresholds) by `gameplay export-c`. ROIs are absolute (fixed rig; chrome registration exists but is unused in v0).
19	- **Stateful tracker (`gp_streak_track`/`gp_streak_reset`, state owned by the caller).** **Presence is binary — not present ⇒ streak reset ⇒ 0** (immediate; the sole reset path). While present, **a confident wheel read is authoritative for its place** (Greg: a clear digit read trumps the rollover logic) — it wins even if the value drops, so a misread is a self-correcting one-frame blip; an unreadable (rolling) wheel is filled (holds last, or resets to 0 when a higher place carried). ≥2 confident wheels seed. This replaced a monotonic forward window `[last, last+30]` whose forward-only search couldn't represent a value below `last` → a tens misread locked the value high (11x read as 14x…); confident-trumps fixes it. Host validation over the 6549-frame capture: hand-read anchors exact (100 % in-sample confident-digit accuracy with the refined 8×15 cells), 0 non-reset decreases, correct slide-gating, max 304.
20	- **Engine + dashboard.** `game_state_t.streak` (new `uint16_t`); the observer holds one tracker (`s_streak`), advances it on `in_song` reads and resets it when gameplay is left; log adds `streak<s>`. Feed applies `DASH_EVT_STREAK` → `ScreenDashboard_ApplyStreak` → `Marvin_LABEL_DASHBOARD_ROBOT_Streak` via a fixed `leFixedString` (shows "0" at reset — see the 2026-07-10 label-clear fix).
21	- **Reset behaviour (w/ Greg).** Score/multiplier/streak zero out **the instant a run is requested** (top of `run()`, before nav/connect), not on reaching gameplay. During the song a **broken streak** (odometer no longer locked) blanks immediately (→ 0). **After the song ends everything stays** (score/multiplier/streak persist on the end screen) — the next run's request is the only reset. `play_until_done` tracks **peak streak** (persists across misses) + **final score** and logs `GC: result score N, peak streak M` — the values `Results_Append` (spec §4.8.6) will persist once that path is wired.
22	- **Known follow-ups (deferred, this commit lands the lock fix first):** (1) **Tens 0↔8 flicker** — the odometer's zero has a center slash; A2D aliasing closes its top loop on ~half the frames, so a tens "0" genuinely matches the **8** template better (4590 vs 6885) and reads 8 *confidently*, alternating frame-to-frame (100↔180, etc.; a hundreds variant flashes 900). Real per-frame ambiguity, not a template bug → fix with a **per-place debounce** (a changed confident digit must persist ≥2 reads before committing; can't lock since it follows reads up or down). (2) **Integer-coverage rewrite** — coverage is still float, so the per-wheel `known` flag can differ C-vs-Python on a borderline wheel (Python `np.round` half-to-even vs C half-up), benign for the tracker; going integer (midpoint threshold + integer grid edges) removes all FP (ARM926 has no FPU) and gives bit-exact parity.
23	- Host cross-check (`test_firmware_classify` `streak`): C == Python on presence + confidence flags + every confident digit, all 47 corpus frames; `test_streak.py` covers the tracker logic. Full gameplay suite **71 passed**; `gameplay_score.c` compiles clean under `cc -Wall -Wextra` via the cross-check driver. Files: `game/gameplay_score.{h,c}`, `game/gameplay_metadata.h` (regen), `game/gameplay_engine.{c,h}`, `game/game_controller.c`, `ui/dashboard_feed.c`, `ui/screens/dashboard/screen_dashboard.{c,h}`. No MCC/Legato hand-edits. **Pending Greg's MPLAB build + hardware validation** (streak label tracks the odometer, holds through single rolls, jumps at carries, blanks at song start / on a miss). Career-font score mode is the only deferred scoring-block item.
24	
25	---
26	
27	**2026-07-08 — SONG card playtime bar wired; song-info widget rename sync.** An MGS regen renamed the SONG-info section and replaced the hand-built progress-bar hack (`panel_Container_63..66_0` / `panel_Text_15/16_0` / `label__0_00_0` / `label__7_22_0_0`) with three named widgets: `LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_START_TIME` (the "0:00" origin marker), `LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_STOP_TIME`, and a real `leProgressBarWidget` `PROGRESSBAR_DASHBOARD_SONG_PLAYTIME`. The renamed detail labels (Title/Artist/Album/Genre/Tier/Duration/Status) already used stable `LABEL_DASHBOARD_SONG_*` names, so only the new widgets needed wiring — dashboard code had no references to the removed decorative names.
28	- **Both time markers are runtime `leFixedString`s** (set up in `song_detail_init` alongside the Status label). `STOP_TIME` tracks the committed selection: `ScreenDashboard_ApplySelection` rewrites it with the song's `m:ss` (same `SongDetail_Duration` string shown in the DURATION field), "-" when unknown. `START_TIME` counts up with elapsed play time (see below); it resets to "0:00" on a fresh selection.
29	- **Bar fill + elapsed marker = playthrough time.** New feed event `DASH_EVT_PLAYTIME` (`u.play_ms`) + `DashboardFeed_PostPlaytime`. `game_controller.c` `play_until_done` posts `0` at play start (resets bar + marker) and elapsed ms each `GC_PLAY_POLL_MS` (~300 ms) poll. The dashboard consumer calls `ScreenDashboard_ApplyPlaytime`, which clamps elapsed to `s_song_len_s` (captured in ApplySelection), rewrites `START_TIME` as `m:ss` (formatted directly so 0 reads "0:00" — `SongDetail_Duration(0)` gives "-"), and drives the bar at **pixel resolution** via `ProgressBarAA_SetPermille` (0-1000) rather than the stock 0-100 `setValue` (unknown duration → empty bar, un-clamped marker). The 0-100 value quantized the 349px-wide bar to ~3.5px steps — for a long song it held still several seconds then hopped; permille advances it by single pixels.
30	- **Rounded (pill) bar ends.** New custom widget `ui/widgets/progressbar_aa/` (`ProgressBarAA_EnableRoundImage`) mirrors `panel_aa`: copies the *full progressbar vtable* (so `setValue` etc. survive), overrides `_paint` to run `AaCorners_RenderRoundImage` after the normal draw — eating the four corners back to the card's `SCHEME_PANEL_GRAY_18181B` BASE (resolved at paint time in the active mode). Radius 4 = half the 8px height → full capsule; the fill's leading cap rounds with it (interior pixels preserved). **The radius is carried by the AA pass, not the widget `cornerRadius`:** the stock classic skin's `drawFill` is a plain square `RectFill`, but its `drawBackground` switches to `FillRoundCornerRect` (ArcFills that overshoot the rect — a track visibly taller than the 8px fill) as soon as the widget `cornerRadius` is nonzero. So the widget keeps `cornerRadius` 0 (stock draws a plain square 8px track) and the AA pass owns the rounding. `ScreenDashboard_Setup` also pins the height to 8 (`setSize`, width preserved via `getWidth`). Added to `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake`.
31	  - **Two-vtable gotcha (why the override first did nothing):** unlike a plain panel (where `panel->fn` *is* the base `widget.fn`), `leProgressBarWidget` holds two pointers to its vtable — its typed `bar->fn` and the base `bar->widget.fn`. The renderer dispatches paint via the *base* `widget.fn->_paint` (it works on a `leWidget*`), so `ProgressBarAA_EnableRoundImage` must repoint **both**; repointing only `bar->fn` leaves the stock paint running and the corners square.
32	  - **Partial-repaint gotcha (fill-end artifacts):** `AaCorners_RenderRoundImage` re-blends existing pixels toward the backdrop and writes at full-rect coordinates via `_Unsafe` pixel ops (relative to the current frame/damage rect, no bounds check). `panel_aa` is safe because a panel repaints its whole rect. But the stock `setValue` damages only the delta strip between old/new value, so a mid-bar update leaves the frame rect a sliver — the corner writes land outside that tile (garbage) and, over many updates, erode the AA bands into the fill (visible in the first/last ~10%). Fix + smoothness in one: the bar is no longer driven by the stock value at all. `ProgressBarAA_SetPermille` stores a 0-1000 fill fraction and invalidates the *whole* widget; `aa_paint` lets the stock skin draw only the (square) track — the widget value stays 0 so the stock fill is skipped — then draws the fill itself as a `RectFill` of the exact pixel width, then rounds the corners. Full-widget repaint every change keeps the corner writes in-bounds and idempotent, and the pixel-width fill removes the 100-step quantization.
33	- **Tier string is stars-only** (separate ask): `SongDetail_TierText` drops the " TIER n" suffix — main-setlist songs show just ★×tier, bonus still "BONUS". Shared helper, so song-select dialog and dashboard both change.
34	- Rides the existing single-consumer/render-lock feed flow — no off-thread widget touch. Files: `ui/screens/dashboard/screen_dashboard.{c,h}`, `ui/dashboard_feed.{c,h}`, `game/game_controller.c`, `ui/widgets/progressbar_aa/*` (new), `ui/song_detail.{c,h}`, `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake`. No MCC/Legato hand-edits (MGS regen staged separately). **Pending Greg's MPLAB build + hardware validation** (stop time matches the selected song; bar fills smoothly over a playthrough and resets on the next run/selection; rounded ends clean with no fill artifacts).

38	**2026-07-07 — Wiimotes screen is now a nav-selectable base view; nav widget rename sync.** An MGS regen renamed the navigation widgets (dropped the `_0` suffix; `BUTTON_NAV_HAMBURGER` → `BUTTON_DASHBOARD_TITLEBAR_NAVIGATION`), gave the wiimotes screen proper names (`Marvin_panel_Marvin` → `Marvin_PANEL_WIIMOTES`, + `PANEL_WIIMOTES_*`/`BUTTON_WIIMOTES_*`), and added a **Wiimotes** nav entry + a titlebar hamburger on the wiimotes screen. Updated code to match and wired the entry.
39	- **Base-view swap (new compositor verb, first real use):** `UiManager_ShowDashboard()`/`UiManager_ShowWiimotes()` swap the BASE hw layer between `CANVAS_DASH` (layer 0) and `CANVAS_WIIMOTES` (layer 4). The outgoing canvas is **hidden first** (`gfxcSetLayer` requires the canvas inactive, and an active canvas drives its layer — two on BASE would fight), then the incoming one is bound. Showing wiimotes hides live video (HEO + OVR1 frame); returning restores it via `ScreenVideo_ShowWindowed()`. Mirrors the song-select open/close video handling.
40	- **Picking across a swap:** Legato picks across *all* attached layers regardless of canvas visibility, so the hidden view's panel must be gated off or it still intercepts touches. `UiManager_SetBaseViewPickable(on)` routes to the active view (`ScreenWiimotes_SetInput` / `UiManager_SetDashboardPickable`). The nav drawer now gates the **active base view** (was dashboard-only) — and because wiimotes is layer 4 (above the drawer's layer 1), gating it off is also what lets the open drawer receive touches over the wiimotes view.
41	- **Both titlebar hamburgers** (dashboard layer 0, wiimotes layer 4) wire to the same drawer toggle; the wiimotes one only picks while its view is shown (its subtree is gated otherwise).
42	- **Wiimotes fret buttons are inputs, not indicators (decided w/ Greg):** the wiimotes screen is for manual / override control, so its `BUTTON_WIIMOTES_ROBOT_FRET_*` are *not* fed by the dashboard feed — they'll drive manual actuation, not mirror activity.
